note: Branch rows (pdf 54): B, the internal-condition rows 1000 S0 cccc and NOPP, each followed by a displacement word. Every expect value is read from the cited page images and derived by hand; none comes from this core, an assembler or another implementation. Targets follow S3.2.2 (pdf 47): forward adds the displacement to PC+2, backward adds its 16-bit one's complement (C50). Source vectors on the 7/9 rows omit cycles (A-05); the cycle counts live only in kind=policy POL-BR-01 vectors (C29). Bus lists stop at the displacement BAR of the one branch figure (pdf 32).

vectors.cite: Branch table, B row, pdf 54; S3.2.2 and Fig 3.2.2, pdf 47; C50; branch timing figure, pdf 32
vectors.derivation: The branch table (pdf 54) prints B as 1000 S0 0000 followed by the displacement word pppppp PPPP PP PPPP, 7/9 cycles: 'Branch unconditional, Program Counter Relative (+1025 to -1024)'. S3.2.2 (pdf 47): the second word is the address displacement; when the destination direction bit (bit 5, printed S on pdf 54, 'S is 0 for +, 1 for -') is zero the displacement is added to PC+2, when it is one the displacement is one's complemented and then added to PC+2 (C50: the 16-bit one's complement of the displacement word; sums wrap at 16 bits); on a false result the program continues with the next sequential instruction, PC+2. Program at $1000: $0200 (bit 5 = 0, forward), displacement $0000. Init S = 1, Z = 1, OV = 1, C = 1. B is unconditional, so it always branches. Forward: the target is PC+2 + displacement = $1002 + $0000 = $1002, the same address the not-taken path would reach. Cycles are not asserted: pdf 54 prints 7/9 without saying which figure applies (C29, A-05); the POL-BR-01 policy vectors carry them. The row has no Not Interruptable note, so prev_interruptible goes 0 -> 1. Bus (pdf 32, the one branch timing figure, drawn for BEXT: BAR 'output program counter', NACT, DTB, NACT, BAR 'output PC+1 to fetch displacement'): FETCH at cycle 0 from $1000; the BAR at cycle 4 puts out $1001, whose word $0000 is the displacement (recorded as a READ). The figure ends there, so no later access is listed. No status bit changes (pdf 54 prints no status change). Registers and memory not named stay unchanged.
